Carla (Acme): Hey, starting ~10:30 UTC today our production API calls to Redwood started returning 401 invalid_api_key. No deploys or code changes on our side; the only recent change was a scheduled key rotation earlier this week.
Maria (Redwood Support): Thanks for reporting — can you share a minimal failing curl and confirm whether this is hosted/dedicated/private for your org? Also: does the request path go through any CDN or edge worker?
Carla (Acme): We're on Dedicated (eu-west). Curl from my laptop succeeds, but the same curl from our Render-hosted backend yields 401. Laptop curl below: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: ApiKey RKz7EXAMPLE_LONG_KEY_abcdef0123456789==" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
```
Carla (Acme): From Render we get HTTP/1.1 401 and body {"error":{"type":"invalid_api_key","message":"Invalid API key"}}
Maria (Redwood Support): Weird that laptop works but backend doesn't. Can you check what the Authorization header length is as observed by your server (log the raw header bytes) and whether there are any proxies between Render and Cloudflare?
Carla (Acme): Laptop header length shows 88 chars. Backend logs only show 64 chars and an ellipsis. We do route via Cloudflare and have a small Worker that strips sensitive headers for static routes — it should not touch the API subdomain.
Eli (Eng): @infra-oncall can you inspect audit logs for the customer key id (rk_...) and also gateway logs for any header parsing warnings from around 10:29-10:35 UTC?
infra-oncall: Audit shows key status ACTIVE and no revoke. Gateway logs show many 401s from two Render egress IPs starting 10:29 UTC. I also see RFC7230 header-parsing warnings and a note about truncated header segments for those connections.
Maria (Redwood Support): Truncated header would explain laptop vs Render. Carla, can you temporarily disable the Cloudflare Worker or bypass CF to test whether the header arrives intact? Even if the Worker is scoped to static paths, config bugs can apply to subdomains.
Carla (Acme): Disabled the Worker for api subdomain and redeployed. Re-tested — backend now receives full Authorization length (88) and requests succeed.
infra-oncall: On our side when Worker was enabled we saw Authorization cut to 64 bytes; with Worker disabled full header passed and authentication accepted.
Eli (Eng): Root cause appears to be the CF Worker code path calling event.request.headers.set() (or otherwise touching the headers) for a non-matching route due to a routing rule bug; the Worker runtime then serialized headers into segments and clipped long values.
Maria (Redwood Support): Short-term: keep the Worker disabled for the api subdomain. Long-term: update the Worker to early-return for /v1/* and add unit tests that verify long Authorization headers pass unchanged. We'll also add a KB note warning customers about edge Workers and header size/normalization pitfalls.
Carla (Acme): Confirmed — disabling Worker fixed the 401s. We'll patch the Worker and test in staging before re-enabling. Appreciate the quick help.
deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-15T11:02:07Z - worker/redact-headers v2 reverted (api rule disabled)
Maria (Redwood Support): Closing loop — marking this as support->eng-infra postmortem candidate so we create the KB and add a checklist for Worker testing. Thanks for the detailed repro, Carla! :thumbsup:
